record.paper_title: Selection Principles in Mathematics: A Milestone of Open Problems
record.original_question: Does there exist, in ZFC, a topological space for which the game G1(D, D) is undetermined, where in inning n player ONE chooses a family U_n of open sets whose union is dense in X, player TWO chooses one set U_n from that family, and TWO wins exactly when the chosen sets still have dense union?

evidence.quote: In the game G1(U, V) ONE chooses in the nth inning an element Un of U and then TWO responds by choosing Un ∈ U n. They play an inning per natural number. A play ... is won by TWO if {Un}n∈ N ∈ V; otherwise ONE wins.
Let D denote the collection of all families U of open sets in X such that ∪U is dense in X.
Problem 13.1 ([8, Question 4.2], [42, footnote 1]) . Does there exist in ZFC a space in which G1(D, D) is undetermined?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $\mathcal{D}$ denote the collection of all families $\mathcal{U}$ of open subsets of $X$ such that $\bigcup\mathcal{U}$ is dense in $X$. Consider the following infinite two-player game $G_1(\mathcal{D},\mathcal{D})$ of length $\omega$: in inning $n\in\mathbb{N}$, player ONE chooses a family $\mathcal{U}_n\in\mathcal{D}$, and player TWO responds by choosing a single set $U_n\in\mathcal{U}_n$. Player TWO wins the play if $\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}} U_n$ is dense in $X$; otherwise ONE wins. The game $G_1(\mathcal{D},\mathcal{D})$ is said to be undetermined on $X$ if neither player has a winning strategy.

Question: Does there exist, provably in ZFC, a topological space $X$ for which the game $G_1(\mathcal{D},\mathcal{D})$ is undetermined?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not turn up a published ZFC construction of a space on which $G_1(\mathcal{D},\mathcal{D})$ is undetermined, nor a proof that no such space exists in ZFC. The question continues to be cited in subsequent literature on selection-principle games, but no resolution was located. Status is therefore recorded as unknown.

status_evidence.title: On some topological games involving networks
status_evidence.snippet: References various selection-principle games G_1(A,B) including dense-open variants without indicating a ZFC resolution of the undeterminedness problem for G_1(D,D).
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on selection-principle games does not record a ZFC resolution of the undeterminedness problem for G_1(D,D).

status_evidence.title: The Story of a Topological Game
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of topological games of Berner–Juhasz type discussing determinacy questions on dense subsets without providing a ZFC example of undeterminedness for G_1(D,D).
status_evidence.claim: Surveys of related games do not assert a ZFC resolution.
